'''''Iberis sempervirens''''', the '''evergreen candytuft'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=IBSE|taxon=Iberis sempervirens|accessdate=22 January 2016}}</ref> or '''perennial candytuft''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Brassicaceae, [[native plant|native]] to southern Europe. The species is often used as an ornamental garden shrub because of its decorative flowers.  ''Iberis'' is so named because many members of the genus come from the [[Iberian Peninsula]] in south west Europe. ''Sempervirens'' means "always green", referring to the evergreen foliage.<ref>{{citation |url = https://hcs.osu.edu/hcs/tmi/plantlist/ib_irens.html|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110512171950/https://hcs.osu.edu/hcs/tmi/plantlist/ib_irens.html |archivedate=May 12, 2011|title=Brassicaceae [also known as Cruciferae] - Mustard Family}}</ref>

==Range==
The natural range is in Europe in [[Spain]], [[France]], [[Italy]], Romania and the [[Balkan Peninsula]]. In Africa, it is found in Morocco and Algeria. In Asia, it is present in Syria and Turkey. It is naturalised in the [[British Isles]], in Assam, and in North America. It grows in [[steppe]]s and [[dry forest]]s on moderately dry to fresh, slightly [[acid]]ic to [[alkaline]], sandy-loamy to [[loamy]], nutrient-rich soils in sunny to light shady locations. The species is heat loving and frost hardy.<ref>Jost Fitschen: Gehölzflora. 12., überarbeitete und ergänzte Auflage. Quelle & Meyer, Wiebelsheim 2007, {{ISBN|3-494-01422-1}}, S. 534.</ref>

==Description==
It is a spreading [[subshrub]] growing to {{convert|30|cm|0|abbr=on}} high by {{convert|40|cm|0|abbr=on}} broad. As an [[ornamental plant]] it is a spring-blooming favourite, often seen cascading over rocks and walls, or used as [[groundcover]]. The glossy, evergreen foliage forms a billowing mound, with many fragrant, pure white flowers in tight clusters <ref name=RHSAZ>{{cite book|title=RHS A-Z encyclopedia of garden plants|year=2008|publisher=Dorling Kindersley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=978-1405332965|pages=1136}}</ref> for several weeks during spring and early summer. The leaf blade of the leaves is leathery, {{cvt|1-3|in|mm|round=5|order=flip|disp=or}} (and rarely {{cvt|5|in|mm|order=flip|round=5|disp=or}}) long, 2 to 5 millimetres wide, oblong [[spatulate]] to lanceolate, obtuse with a pointed base. The fruits are roundish to broad ovate, 6 to 8 millimetres long and 5 to 6 millimetres wide. The seeds are narrowly winged and 2 to 3 millimetres long.<ref>Andreas Roloff, Andreas Bärtels: Flora der Gehölze. Bestimmung, Eigenschaften und Verwendung. Mit einem Winterschlüssel von Bernd Schulz. 3., korrigierte Auflage. Eugen Ulmer, Stuttgart (Hohenheim) 2008, {{ISBN|978-3-8001-5614-6}}, S. 346.</ref>

==Cultivation==
When grown in a garden it may require light pruning right after blooming, but otherwise plants can be left alone in fall and early spring. It is drought-tolerant once established. It prefers a well-drained site, so heavy clay soils that stay wet in winter should be avoided. It is not easily divided.<ref>{{cite web|title=Iberis sempervirens|url=http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/gardens-gardening/your-garden/plant-finder/plant-details/kc/k620/iberis-sempervirens.aspx|website=Missouri Botanical Garden|accessdate=12 October 2017}}</ref> ''Iberis sempervirens'' survives in [[Hardiness zone|USDA hardiness zones]] 3–9 with mean annual minimum temperatures of {{cvt|-10|to|-5|F|C|order=flip}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/all/iberis-sempervirens/|title=Iberis sempervirens|website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu|access-date=2017-01-07}}</ref>

It is hardy in most parts of the UK, surviving temperatures down to {{convert|-15|C|F|abbr=on}}. [[Vernalization]] (a period of cold weather) is required for flower initiation.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://flor.hrt.msu.edu/assets/PdfAttachments/Vernalizationpart7.pdf|title=Vernalization: Life In The Cold|last=|first=|date=January 2006|website=|publisher=Greenhouse Grower|access-date=2017-01-06}}</ref>  At least 8–10 weeks are needed at an average temperature of {{cvt|5|C|F|-1}}.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ballseed.com/media/Culture/PAS/Iberis_Whiteout_Kieft.pdf|title=Whiteout Iberis|last=|first=|date=2013|website=|publisher=Ball Horticultural Company|access-date=2017-01-06|archive-date=2017-01-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170107172509/http://www.ballseed.com/media/Culture/PAS/Iberis_Whiteout_Kieft.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The [[cultivar]] 'Snowflake'<ref>{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/104665/Iberis-sempervirens-Snowflake/Details |publisher=Royal Horticultural Society|accessdate=28 March 2020}}</ref> has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web  | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 52 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate = 3 March 2018}}</ref>
